name: ProposalCraft

hlido_opinion.headline: An MCP server that drafts client proposals in your own voice, learned from ones that already won — tightly scoped, local-only, and honest that it is a launch-day project.
hlido_opinion.body: ProposalCraft is an MCP server for freelancers and agencies: paste a client brief into Claude and it drafts a send-ready proposal — structured, scoped and priced — in the voice learned from proposals that previously won you work. The scoping is its strength. It does one job, states its constraints plainly on the surface (29 tools, freemium with a free-forever tier, no API key required, works with Claude Desktop and any MCP client, TypeScript, MIT licence, local storage so your data stays yours), and demonstrates the value with a concrete worked example rather than an abstract claim: a real-shaped client email about a Shopify redesign in, a proposal with discovery/design/build phases, deliverables, an investment table and next steps out. Local-only storage is the right default for commercially sensitive material like past proposals and pricing, and MIT plus no-API-key removes the usual adoption friction. Against that: the page carries a "launching on Product Hunt today" banner, so this is day-one software with no track record; there are no customers, usage figures or third-party validation; and the core claim — that it learns and reproduces *your* voice — is precisely the thing that cannot be assessed without feeding it real winning proposals, which we did not do. Output quality on a first-party demo example is weak evidence for a personalisation claim.

tier_rationale: FADING (68) — well-scoped, sensibly defaulted (local storage, MIT, no API key) and demonstrated with a concrete worked example rather than an abstraction. Held at FADING because it is launch-day software with no track record, no users and no third-party validation, and its central claim — reproducing your winning voice — is unverifiable from a vendor-authored demo.
what_it_does_well: Tightly scoped to one job — brief in, send-ready proposal out — with no feature sprawl
Local storage by default: past proposals and pricing never leave the machine
No API key required, MIT licensed, free-forever tier — minimal adoption friction
Concrete worked example (real-shaped brief → structured proposal with phases, deliverables, investment table)
29 MCP tools; works with Claude Desktop and any MCP client
States its constraints openly on the landing page rather than burying them
what_it_fails_at: Launch-day project (Product Hunt banner live) — no track record whatsoever
No customers, usage figures, or third-party validation
The core personalisation claim is unverifiable from a vendor-authored demo
Proposal quality depends entirely on the corpus of past proposals a user supplies — unaddressed on the surface
Freemium boundary is not specified: what the free-forever tier excludes is unclear
Not tested by us with real winning proposals, which is the only meaningful test
best_for: Freelancers and small agencies who write similar proposals repeatedly
Claude Desktop users who want drafting inside their existing workflow
Anyone unwilling to upload commercially sensitive pricing to a cloud service
not_recommended_for: Teams needing collaborative review, approvals or version control on proposals
Buyers who require a track record before trusting client-facing output
Users without a body of past proposals for it to learn from

evidence_urls.claim: MCP server drafting proposals from a client brief, in the user's learned voice
29 tools, TypeScript, MIT licence, no API key required
Local storage — user data stays on the machine
Launching on Product Hunt on the day of review — no track record

agent_relevance.agent_integration_path: MCP-native: 29 tools invoked from Claude Desktop or any MCP client, with no separate UI. The agent does the drafting inside the user's existing assistant.

checklist.evidence: Freemium, free-forever tier; boundary not specified
Detailed worked example; vendor-authored, no third-party proof
